correctness.rationale: For fixed reference R and nonempty target s, a joined-history optimal first phrase cannot cross R/target join because target history initially empty. Every later joined-history phrase has source entirely in R or decoded prefix, or crosses the boundary once and splits into at most two legal source phrases; hence P<=A<=2P-1. Greedy longest-available-match optimality follows from a suffix-of-existing-source exchange that preserves decoded source availability. With pairwise distinct letters R=a1...am, recursively T1=R, Tj=Tj-1(a_j...a_m)Tj-1, the joined parse takes one phrase per stage; unique new a_m a_(j-1) backward adjacency forces two longest split-source phrases at each later stage, so P=m, A=2m-1, length (m-1)2^m+1. Independently recomputed exact dynamic-programming optimum for m=1,...,5: (P,A)=(1,1),(2,3),(3,5),(4,7),(5,9). Proof, not finite search, covers every m.
